script:
Hello, this is The Portfolio Podcast for MEME. Friday — here is your MEME recap. The portfolio closed four point two one percent up on the session. A strong finish to the week, driven by outsized moves in several key names.

Applied Optoelectronics surged again Friday, and this time a well-known short seller stepped in publicly to fade the move. The position is now under scrutiny from both sides of the trade.

No macro news was available for Friday's session. Without a specific index-level print confirmed for the day, the broad market backdrop remains the context in which space, optical networking, and bitcoin mining names traded in sharply divergent directions — some sectors catching a bid, others selling off on earnings disappointment.

Applied Optoelectronics reported second-quarter twenty twenty-six results that beat estimates, with revenues rising eighty-six point four percent year over year to one hundred ninety-one point nine two million dollars, up from one hundred two point nine five million a year earlier. The company posted its fifth consecutive quarter of record revenue, driven by strong demand for its eight hundred gigabit and one point six terabit AI-focused optical transceivers. However, net loss widened to twenty-two point seven eight million dollars, and loss per share increased to twenty-eight cents from sixteen cents. Despite the beat, former hedge fund manager Martin Shkreli posted on X that he is shorting Applied Optoelectronics on the pop, calling it a commodity bottleneck that does not make a great company. That counternarrative is now live in the market. The stock closed up nine point one nine percent on the session.

Applied Optoelectronics was up nine point one nine percent on the session, the second-largest gain across the primary holdings on Friday. Beyond the earnings beat and short seller commentary already covered, the equity inducement grant disclosed Friday — one thousand forty-eight shares to four new employees — signals ongoing hiring activity, a minor but notable operational data point. Watch next week's volume and short interest data closely given the public short position now on record.

Turning to Redwire Corporation, the stock surged fourteen point eight eight percent on the session, the single largest gain in the portfolio on Friday. State Street disclosed a passive stake of seven point three percent in a thirteen-G filing Friday, which added institutional weight to a name already moving on second-quarter twenty twenty-six earnings. The call transcript surfaced Thursday evening, and the combination of earnings momentum and a major passive holder entering the register drove what one headline called a record-breaking week — up more than fifty-five percent over the five days.

Over at AST SpaceMobile, the stock gained six point eight zero percent on the session. A Wall Street upgrade described as flipping the narrative on space stocks broadly pulled the sector higher, with reporting noting SpaceX-related names and peers all catching a bid simultaneously. Fresh institutional interest ahead of a critical earnings execution update was also flagged. Watch the upcoming earnings print for concrete network deployment progress.

Nebius Group fell one point zero one percent on the session. No company-specific news drove the move; the mild pullback appears consistent with broader profit-taking in AI infrastructure names after recent outperformance.

Bloom Energy dropped four point two zero percent on the session. No company-specific catalyst was identified. The move tracks weakness seen across select industrial and energy names on Friday.

Meanwhile, TeraWulf slid three point zero six percent on the session. Reporting Friday tied the move directly to second-quarter earnings results, with losses outweighing any support from Bitcoin holding near sixty-five thousand dollars. The headline noted this was among the worst weeks in months for several bitcoin mining names purely on earnings fundamentals.

Lumentum Holdings gained six point two two percent on the session. The stock was flagged in weekend watch lists alongside Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway and Cisco as names with pending catalysts. Earnings are on the near-term calendar — that report is the key event to monitor.

Turning to IREN Limited, the stock rose eight point seven zero percent on the session. No company-specific news drove the move directly, though the gain tracks a broader recovery pattern in compute infrastructure and bitcoin mining-adjacent names that held up better than peers on Friday.

Finally, Sandisk Corporation fell three point six eight percent on the session. No specific news was identified for the name on Friday. The pullback is consistent with mixed action in storage and memory-adjacent technology, and the next significant catalyst will be any guidance update or sector-level demand signal from the flash storage market.

Three items to watch in the next forty-eight hours. First, Lumentum Holdings earnings — flagged for imminent release, and given the six point two two percent move on Friday, the actual print will either confirm or challenge that momentum. Second, Bitcoin price action heading into the weekend: with TeraWulf and IREN both sensitive to the coin, any break from sixty-five thousand dollars in either direction has direct read-through. Third, short interest data on Applied Optoelectronics — with a named short seller publicly on record, the next positioning update will indicate whether institutional shorts are piling in behind that call.

This is The Portfolio Podcast for MEME. We will be back same time the next business day with tomorrow's news. Watch Lumentum's earnings and any follow-through on the Redwire institutional filing — both have the potential to set the tone for the week ahead.
